correctness.rationale: After diagonalizing A, the two positive Gram matrices |AB|^2 and |BA|^2 have the same two-point spectrum. Two-dimensional functional calculus gives an exact divided-difference formula, and a direct determinant expansion yields a gap whose sign is exactly sign(kp), with the stated commutation equality case.

originality.rationale: Prior work proves the k=2 Hermitian comparison and partial arbitrary-k parameter ranges, while the 2022 thesis explicitly leaves the broader comparison as a conjecture. Targeted searches, including the 2026 normal-matrix extension, did not locate the exact 2×2 all-real-exponent phase law. Residual risk from older low-dimensional matrix-inequality literature remains, so the claim is to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp exact gap formula, simultaneously resolves the positive- and negative-exponent formulations in order two, and identifies commutation as the exact equality boundary.
